approachQuestion.prompt:
Assigning calibration booths

There are n appointments [start,end), each with a unique input index. Assign each appointment a booth ID so appointments in the same booth never overlap, using the fewest booths. Return the number of booths and an ID array in input order. Any optimal assignment is accepted. Input order is arbitrary and immutable. An appointment ending at t may share a booth with one starting at t.

Input: appointments = [[5,8],[1,4],[3,6],[8,9]]
Output: count = 2, ids = [1,1,2,1]

Input: appointments = [[1,2],[2,3]]
Output: count = 1, ids = [1,1]

Constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000; integer endpoints satisfy 0 ≤ start < end ≤ 1000000000. IDs are integers from 1 through the returned count. Choose the best comparison-based worst-case running time. Assignments, not only the count, are required.

options.text: Sort copied appointment records by start, retaining original indices. Keep a min-heap with one (latestEnd,boothId) per allocated booth. If its smallest end is at most the next start, reuse that booth and replace its end; otherwise allocate a new booth. Write each ID at its original index.
options.feedback: If the earliest booth is still occupied, every allocated booth is occupied and another is necessary. Otherwise reusing an available booth preserves feasibility. Original indices restore the required answer order.

options.text: Sort by start and remember only the booth of the immediately previous appointment. Reuse it when free; otherwise allocate a new booth.
options.feedback: For [[1,3],[2,10],[4,5]], the first booth is free for [4,5) although the last-started appointment still runs. This allocates 3 booths when 2 suffice.

options.text: Count the maximum simultaneous appointments from ordered endpoint events and return that number with no per-appointment IDs.
options.feedback: The peak is the right minimum count, but the contract also requires a valid assignment for every original input index. A count alone is an incomplete result.

options.text: Sort by start. For each appointment, linearly inspect every allocated booth end until finding a free booth; allocate only if all are occupied. Record original-index assignments.
options.feedback: This is correct and can find a minimum assignment, but it may scan every allocated booth for each appointment. A priority queue exposes the earliest available booth without repeated full scans.

feedback.reason: Turn an interval resource lower bound into an actual optimal assignment by reusing the earliest-free resource.
details: Copy appointment records with original indices, sort them using iterative bottom-up merge sort, and assign booths using an iterative binary min-heap of (end,id). Heap arrays are preallocated for n records. Replace the minimum end on reuse or insert a new booth. Write IDs directly to the returned array.

Reuse the booth whose current appointment ends earliest when its end permits the new start. Preserve original indices for output IDs. A heap of ends answers availability; sorting only by duration cannot maintain chronological reuse.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For reuse-earliest-booth, n is the appointment count. Count copied records, sorting buffer and heap as auxiliary storage; exclude the returned assignment array and count. Choose the tightest standard worst-case pair.
constraints: Analyze only the named method. Count all temporary arrays and the call stack; exclude the supplied input and returned output. Numeric comparisons, assignments and arithmetic take constant time, with no overflow.
No hashing or amortized data structure is used. All loops and binary searches are iterative; there is no recursive stack.

options.text: Time O(n log n), auxiliary space O(n)
Time O(n log n), auxiliary space O(1)

feedback.reason: Sort indexed appointments and perform one logarithmic heap update per appointment.
details: Sorting costs O(n log n). Each appointment performs at most one insertion or root replacement in a binary heap of at most n booths, also bounded by O(n log n) overall. The copy, reusable sorting buffer and heap are linear auxiliary memory. Preallocation makes no amortized append assumption necessary.
Iterative merge sort and heap; preallocated arrays; original-index output excluded.
“Time O(n), auxiliary space O(n)”: Both comparison sorting and heap maintenance may take logarithmic work per appointment, so linear total time omits required operations.
“Time O(n log n), auxiliary space O(1)”: The copied records, merge buffer and booth heap are auxiliary arrays even though the assignment array itself is excluded.
“Time O(n²), auxiliary space O(n)”: No full scan of all booths is performed for each appointment. The heap provides the earliest end with logarithmic updates.
